paraphrase: All buddhas and sentient beings are only the one mind; there is no other dharma. This mind has since beginningless time never been born or perished; it is neither blue nor yellow, without form, beyond existence and non-existence, new and old, long and short; it is like space. This one mind is buddha; buddha and beings are not different — beings seek outside with forms and lose it; 'using the buddha to seek the buddha, using the mind to grasp the mind'.

original.text: 諸佛與一切眾生。唯是一心。更無別法。此心無始已來。不曾生不曾滅

paraphrase: In this one mind not a speck of dharma can be attained; this very mind is buddha. Making offerings to all buddhas of the ten directions is not as good as offering to one person of the Way without mind (wuxin daoren).

original.text: 唯此一心更無微塵許法可得。即心是佛

paraphrase: Only be without mind (wuxin) and that is the ultimate; if students of the Way do not become without mind right now, they will not accomplish the Way however many kalpas they practise; some attain no-mind on hearing the Dharma in a single thought, others only after the ten stages — the attainment is the same, the latter only suffered longer.

original.text: 但能無心。便是究竟。學道人若不直下無心。累劫修行終不成道

paraphrase: At the time of death one should only contemplate that the five aggregates are empty and the four elements without self; the true mind is formless, neither coming nor going; if auspicious signs of buddhas coming to welcome appear, do not follow them; if frightening signs appear, do not fear them; only forget the mind and be one with the dharma-realm.

original.text: 凡人臨欲終時。但觀五蘊皆空四大無我。真心無相不去不來
